links.outcome: Local ambient scribe effect on time-in-note, burnout, task load, accuracy, and usability versus control
links.effect: Nabla reduced time-in-note 9.5% (95% CI -17.2% to -1.8%; P=0.02); DAX no significant change (-1.7%). Both scribes suggested improved Mini-Z, task load, and work exhaustion; occasional inaccuracies reported.
links.quote: Nabla users experienced a 9.5% (95% CI, -17.2% to -1.8%; P=0.02) decrease in time-in-note versus the control group, whereas DAX users exhibited no significant change versus the control group (-1.7%; 95% CI, -9.4% to +5.9%; P=0.66).

links.outcome: Clinician-reported clinically significant inaccuracies in ambient scribe notes
links.effect: Clinically significant inaccuracies noted 'occasionally' on five-point Likert questions (DAX 2.7 [95% CI 2.4 to 3.0]; Nabla 2.8 [95% CI 2.6 to 3.0]).
links.quote: One grade 1 (mild) adverse event was reported, while clinically significant inaccuracies were noted "occasionally" on five-point Likert questions (DAX 2.7 [95% CI, 2.4 to 3.0]; Nabla 2.8 [95% CI, 2.6 to 3.0]).

links.outcome: Documentation time and clinician burnout after AI scribe deployment using validated instruments
links.effect: Improvements in Mini-Z (DAX +2.83; Nabla +2.69), PTL (DAX -39.9), and PFI-WE (DAX -0.32; Nabla -0.23) versus control; Nabla reduced time-in-note 9.5%.
links.quote: Increases in total Mini-Z (scale 10-50; DAX 2.83 [95% CI, +1.28 to +4.37]; Nabla +2.69 [95% CI, +1.14 to +4.23]) and reductions in PTL (scale 0-400; DAX -39.9 [95% CI, -71.9 to -7.9]; Nabla -31.7 [95% CI, -63.8 to +0.4]), and PFI-WE (scale 0-4; DAX 0.32 [95% CI,-0.55 to -0.08]; Nabla -0.23 [95% CI, -0.46 to +0.01]) scores suggest improvement for users of either scribe versus the control.

screen.reason: This is a pragmatic randomized controlled trial evaluating the deployment of two ambient AI scribe tools (DAX Copilot and Nabla) versus usual care among outpatient physicians in real clinical practice, assessing documentation time, burnout, and safety/accuracy.
